header.userPrompt:
Implement the follow-ups from GitHub issue #196 (https://github.com/VirtusLab/orca/issues/196). All items are in scope. Where the issue leaves a choice open (item 2: start logging later vs. move the file; item 4: keep or drop AttemptOutcome; item 6: probe claude's sandbox /tmp access), make the call in the plan and state the reason. Issue text:

Follow-ups from #193 (on-disk layout of run and attempt state). Each is independent.

### 1. `BackendTag.wireName` is compatibility code

Its scaladoc says it exists so "a future rename can't silently strand every persisted session". #193 withdrew that rule. Today `SessionCommitted.harness` is a `String`, the manifest stores it, and three readers (`FlowLifecycle.targetAgent`, `ResumeCommand`, `SessionPicker`) parse it back with `fromWireName`, each with an "unknown harness" branch.

Fix: carry `BackendTag` on the event and in the manifest with a derived codec. Delete `wireName`, `fromWireName`, `BackendTagCodecTest` and the three branches.

### 2. The trace log lives in the system temp dir

`$TMPDIR/orca-<n>.log` holds every prompt and agent reply, grows without bound across runs, and is the only orca file outside `.orca/` or an XDG dir. The natural home is `.orca/cache/attempts/<id>.log`, pruned with the manifest.

The catch: `OrcaLog.start()` runs at the top of `flow()`, before `resolveRunDir` decides where the run happens. Either start logging after that (and lose the lines about worktree resolution) or move the file once the directory is known.

### 3. `RecoveryCheck`'s branch-ref helpers belong in `FeatureBranch`

`isSafeBranchRef`, `isSafeReusedRef` and `alwaysProtected` are used by `FeatureBranch` and `FlowLifecycle` on fresh runs too, so "recovery" misnames them. Pure move; about 30 test lines follow.

### 4. `AttemptOutcome` / `AttemptStatus` round trip

`flow.scala` tracks an `AttemptStatus`, narrows it to `AttemptOutcome` for `finish`, and the writer widens it back. Passing `AttemptStatus` deletes one enum and one mapping, at the cost that `finish(Running)` compiles. Kept narrow in #193 on purpose; decide.

### 5. Two XDG resolvers

`ConfigHome` (config dir, `tools`) and `BuiltInFlows.cacheHome` (cache dir, `shell`) implement the same fallback rule. One `XdgDirs` in `tools` should own both.

### 6. Smaller items

- `ClaudeBackend.writeMcpConfig` puts `mcp-<id>.json` in `.orca/cache/` because, its comment says, a sandboxed claude cannot read `/tmp`. Yet claude's system-prompt file is read from `/tmp` every turn. Probe live, then fix the comment or the location.
- The claude MCP config JSON is built by string interpolation without escaping; gemini's equivalent uses a codec. Make them agree.
- `GeminiSettings` restores `.gemini/settings.json` on close but leaves the `.gemini/` directory it created; a stage commit during an open interactive conversation sweeps the modified file in.
- `FlowAuthoring.extractApiMaterial` keeps an idempotency check and a per-file atomic write that cannot trigger in a fresh sandbox.
- `SessionRecord` is defined inside `SessionStore.scala` but built from `Session.scala` and six tests; give it its own file.
- Never pruned: session records of a run that never succeeds, orphaned `mcp-*.json` after a hard kill, per-version built-in flow caches, failed authoring sandboxes. All small; the trace log (item 2) is the only one that matters.

resultJson.description:
Close the follow-ups that #193 (on-disk layout of run and attempt state) left in GitHub issue #196. The theme is "one home per fact": the backend tag travels as its own type instead of a string that three readers re-parse; the trace log joins the other attempt files under `.orca/cache/attempts/` and is pruned with them; the branch-ref predicates live with the type that uses them; one XDG resolver serves config and cache; and a handful of small leftovers (a string-built JSON file, a directory left behind, dead idempotency code, a type in the wrong file) are cleaned up.

Where the issue left a choice open, the plan decides: (item 2) logging starts inside `runIn`, after `resolveRunDir`, once the attempt id is known, rather than moving a live logback file — the only lines lost are the pre-resolution ones, whose failure case already reaches stderr in full, and a stop/move/re-attach of a rolling appender adds a drop window and a second rolling-pattern derivation for little value; (item 4) `AttemptOutcome` stays, because `finish(Running)` being unrepresentable is worth more than one three-line mapping, and the round trip is removed on the `flow.scala` side by tracking the outcome directly; (item 6) the claude MCP config moves to the system temp dir like the system-prompt file, gated by a live probe — both files are read by the same claude process from argv, and the system-prompt file has been read from `/tmp` on every turn, so the "sandboxed claude cannot read /tmp" rationale is almost certainly wrong. The "never pruned" list gets no new pruning: session records are keyed by prompt and their progress log is branch-dependent, so no local signal says a run is dead; per-version flow caches and failed authoring sandboxes are small and already documented as kept. The AGENTS.md disk table stays the authoritative map and is updated in the tasks that move files.

tasks.title: Give SessionRecord its own file
tasks.description: Move `case class SessionRecord` (with its scaladoc and the `key` method) out of `flow/src/main/scala/orca/sessions/SessionStore.scala` into a new `flow/src/main/scala/orca/sessions/SessionRecord.scala`, same package and visibility. `SessionStore.scala` keeps the trait, `OsSessionStore` and its codec. No behaviour change; no call site changes, since the package is unchanged. Verify `sbt "flow/test" "runner/test"` still compiles and passes, and run `sbt scalafmtAll`.

tasks.title: Carry BackendTag as a type on the event, the manifest and the session record
tasks.description:
Delete the string round trip for the backend tag (issue #196 item 1).

- `BackendTag` becomes a plain `enum BackendTag: case ClaudeCode, Codex, Opencode, Pi, Gemini` with a companion `given codec: ConfiguredJsonValueCodec[BackendTag]` derived with `CodecMakerConfig.withDiscriminatorFieldName(None)` (the `AttemptStatus` pattern; cases serialise as their names, which is today's spelling). Delete `wireName`, `fromWireName`, the scaladoc about renames, and `tools/src/test/scala/orca/agents/BackendTagCodecTest.scala`.
- `OrcaEvent.SessionCommitted.harness: BackendTag` (emit `backend.tag` in `TurnAccounting.sessionCommitted`); `ManifestSession.harness: BackendTag` (manifest codec picks the companion given up); `SessionRecord.backend: Option[BackendTag]`. In `Session.scala` compare and store `agent.backendTag` directly; `warnBackendSwap` takes the tags and renders them.
- Delete the three unknown-harness branches: `FlowLifecycle.targetAgent` becomes `record.backend.fold(lead)(ctx.agentFor)` and `rehydrateSessions` loses its skip-with-warning arm (keep the invalid-id arm); `ResumeCommand.wireIdAndTag` keeps only the wireId-absent `Left`; `SessionPicker.harnessSettingsName(tag: BackendTag): String` with no fallback. Make `AgentSpec.harnessNameFor` a total function (exhaustive `match`, with `harnessNames` derived from it) so `ResumeCommand.build` and the picker need no `getOrElse`.
- Replace the remaining `.wireName` uses (`EnforcementNotice`, `EnforcementTableTest`) with `.toString`; the rendered AGENTS.md enforcement table is unchanged.
- An unrecognised harness in a manifest now fails decode: add a `ManifestReaderTest` case mirroring the existing "unrecognised outcome" one (skipped with a warning naming the file) and delete `FlowLifecycleTest` "skips a record with an unknown backend tag", `ResumeCommandTest` "an unrecognised harness string is not resumable", `MainTest` "falls back to the raw harness string". Update every fixture and literal listed in the brief to `BackendTag` values, including `AttemptManifestWriterTest`'s raw-JSON `"harness":"claude"` seed (respell `ClaudeCode`, or the pruning tests silently change meaning).
- Update prose: `SessionStore`/`SessionRecord`, `AgentSpec`, `SessionPicker`, `ResumeCommand` scaladocs and AGENTS.md's rehydration sentence (untagged records go to the lead; a tag is a typed value now). Leave dated docs alone. Run `sbt test` and `sbt scalafmtAll`.

tasks.title: Track the attempt outcome in flow() and keep finish's input narrow
tasks.description:
Decision for issue #196 item 4: keep `AttemptOutcome` (a `finish(Running)` that cannot compile is worth more than one mapping) and remove the redundant narrowing on the `flow.scala` side instead.

In `runner/src/main/scala/orca/flowEntry.scala`: `runIn(dir)` returns `AttemptOutcome`; inside it track `var outcome: Option[AttemptOutcome] = None` (set `Some(Succeeded)` after `runFlow` returns, `Some(Failed)` in both catch arms) and call `manifestWriter.finish(outcome.getOrElse(AttemptOutcome.Failed))` in the `finally`, with a one-line comment that `None` is only a fatal throwable escaping the `NonFatal` catch. The `resolveRunDir` refusal arm yields `AttemptOutcome.Failed`; the exit check becomes `if outcome == AttemptOutcome.Failed then System.exit(1)`. Drop the `AttemptStatus` import from `flowEntry.scala` — `AttemptStatus` remains the persisted enum used only by the manifest writer (`statusOf`), reader and shell. Update `AttemptOutcome`'s scaladoc so it states the present contract without history. No test changes expected beyond compilation; run `sbt "runner/test" "shell/test"` and `sbt scalafmtAll`.

tasks.title: Move the trace log under .orca/cache/attempts and prune it with the manifest
tasks.description:
Issue #196 item 2. Decision: start logging inside `runIn` once the attempt id exists, rather than moving a live logback file. The only lines lost are the pre-resolution ones (the `user prompt` line is re-emitted after start; a worktree refusal already reaches stderr in full).

- `OrcaDir`: add `TraceLogSuffix = ".trace.log"` and the rolled sibling suffix `".trace.1.log"`, `traceLogPath(workDir, id)`, and teach `attemptIdOf` both suffixes so `AttemptPruning` deletes them with the manifest. Cover in `OrcaDirTest`.
- Make the `AttemptId` the one home for `startedAt`/`pid`: `flow()` computes `startedAt`, `pid`, `attemptId` inside `runIn` and passes them to `AttemptManifestWriter.start`/`AttemptManifestWriterState` (which stop calling `clock()` for `startedAt`; tests' `newWriter` builds the id from the fixed clock's first instant). Do not derive the id in two places.
- `OrcaLog.start(file: os.Path): OrcaLog` takes the target path (dir already ensured via `OrcaDir.ensureAttempts(dir)`), keeps the 4 MB `FixedWindowRollingPolicy` with pattern `<id>.trace.%i.log`, keeps the best-effort `None` when logback isn't bound. Rewrite the `MaxTraceFileSize` rationale (bounds what one attempt leaves in the cache; pruning bounds the count) and the class scaladoc; fix `logback.xml`'s header comment. `OrcaLogTest` passes a temp path.
- In `flow()`: `resolveRunDir` runs first; inside `runIn`, start the log, print `OrcaBanner`, log the user prompt and the "orca <version> starting (workDir=…)" line, then build the manifest writer; `orcaLog.finish()` moves into `runIn`'s outer `finally`. The refusal arm prints only its `[orca]` line.
- Add a pruning test: a `<id>.trace.log` (and a rolled `.trace.1.log`) of an evicted attempt is deleted; update `AttemptPruning`'s "up to two files" scaladoc.
- AGENTS.md disk table: replace the `$TMPDIR/orca-<n>.log` row with `.orca/cache/attempts/<id>.trace.log (+ .trace.1.log)`, class cache, removed by pruning with its manifest. While there, make the "Removed by" cells for session records, built-in flow caches and authoring sandboxes state explicitly that nothing else prunes them (the issue's last bullet; no pruning is added). Run `sbt test` and `sbt scalafmtAll`.

tasks.title: Move the branch-ref predicates from RecoveryCheck to FeatureBranch
tasks.description: Issue #196 item 3, a pure move. Relocate `isSafeBranchRef`, `isSafeReusedRef` and `alwaysProtected` from `flow/src/main/scala/orca/progress/RecoveryCheck.scala` into `object FeatureBranch` in `FeatureBranch.scala`, keeping their scaladocs (rewritten to cite `FeatureBranch.*`, present tense, no history). `RecoveryCheck.validateHeader` and `FeatureBranch.resolveWith` call the new homes; `FlowLifecycle.scala:375` uses `FeatureBranch.alwaysProtected`; `BranchNamingTest` asserts against `FeatureBranch.isSafeBranchRef`. Move the predicate tests (`RecoveryCheckTest` lines 9-54) into `FeatureBranchTest` unchanged in scenario, leaving `RecoveryCheckTest` with the `validateHeader` cases; fix the two comments naming the old home (`RecoveryCheckTest:102`, `FlowLifecycleTest:3642`). Update scaladoc cross-references in `FeatureBranch.scala` (`UnsafeBranchRefRefused`, the type doc) and `RecoveryCheck`'s object doc. Run `sbt "flow/test" "runner/test"` and `sbt scalafmtAll`.

tasks.title: Introduce XdgDirs in tools as the single XDG base-directory resolver
tasks.description: Issue #196 item 5. Add `tools/src/main/scala/orca/XdgDirs.scala`: `private[orca] object XdgDirs` with `configHome(env: String => Option[String], home: os.Path): os.Path` (`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, fallback `home / ".config"`) and `cacheHome(env, home): os.Path` (`XDG_CACHE_HOME`, fallback `home / ".cache"`), both applying the one rule — a relative, empty or root-climbing value falls back like an unset one — implemented once in a private helper. `ConfigHome.resolve` becomes `ConfigHome(XdgDirs.configHome(env, home) / "orca")`. Delete `BuiltInFlows.cacheHome`; `BuiltInFlows.extracted` and `FlowLauncher.resolveWorkspaceDir` call `XdgDirs.cacheHome`, and their scaladocs cite it instead of "mirroring ConfigHome". Tests: a new `tools/src/test/scala/orca/XdgDirsTest.scala` covering set / unset / relative / empty / root-climbing for both variables; `ConfigHomeTest` keeps only the `/orca` suffix case; `BuiltInFlowsTest`'s relative-`XDG_CACHE_HOME` case may stay as the integration of the two. Run `sbt "tools/test" "shell/test"` and `sbt scalafmtAll`.

tasks.title: Probe claude's /tmp access, then move the MCP config to a temp file built through a codec
tasks.description:
Issue #196 item 6, first two bullets. Decision: the config moves to the system temp dir like the system-prompt file, because the same claude process reads both from argv and the system-prompt file has been read from `/tmp` on every turn; the probe is the gate.

1. Probe live, with the installed `claude`: write an MCP config to `/tmp` naming an `http` server and run `claude -p` with `--mcp-config /tmp/<file>` (with claude's sandbox enabled via its settings if the CLI offers it; check `claude --help`), confirming from claude's own output/debug log that the server was loaded from that path. Record the CLI version, date and outcome in the scaladoc of the code that depends on it.
2. If the probe confirms (expected): `writeMcpConfig` returns `os.temp(prefix = "orca-mcp-", suffix = ".json", contents = …)` with the same lifecycle as `writeSystemPrompt` (released via `SubprocessSpawn.deleteFileResource`); delete `ClaudeBackend.mcpConfigPath`, the `OrcaDir.ensureCache` and `os.remove` steps, and the test "an MCP config left behind by a hard kill can't reach a commit" (replace with one asserting the config path is outside `workDir`). Update `AskUserSession`'s scaladoc and the AGENTS.md disk table (drop the `.orca/cache/mcp-<session id>.json` row; add the MCP config to the `$TMPDIR/orca-*` per-turn IPC row). This also removes the "orphaned mcp-*.json after a hard kill" item.
   If the probe refutes it: keep the location, rewrite the scaladoc to state the probed fact, and add a prune of stale `mcp-*.json` at attempt start (the workdir flow lock makes that safe).
3. Either way, build the JSON through a typed codec, agreeing with `GeminiSettings`: `private case class McpServerEntry(`type`: String, url: String, timeout: Long)` and a `mcpServers: Map[String, McpServerEntry]` wrapper via `JsonCodecMaker.make`; delete `entryJson`. Add a `ClaudeBackendTest` case that a server URL containing `"` or `\` yields valid JSON (parse it back), mirroring `GeminiSettingsTest` "merge escapes a URL containing JSON metacharacters". Run `sbt "claude/test"` and `sbt scalafmtAll`.

tasks.title: Remove the .gemini directory GeminiSettings created and state the mid-turn commit residual
tasks.description: Issue #196 item 6, third bullet. In `GeminiSettings.register`, record whether `<workDir>/.gemini` existed before the write; on close, after restoring or removing `settings.json`, remove the directory too when it did not exist before and is now empty (an unexpected extra file leaves it in place). Add two `GeminiSettingsTest` cases: close removes a `.gemini/` it created; close keeps a pre-existing `.gemini/`. Extend the object scaladoc with the present-tense fact that the modified file sits in the user's tree for the turn, so a commit the agent itself makes mid-turn includes it (orca's own stage commits run after the turn's restore) — the residual is documented, not fixed. Run `sbt "gemini/test"` and `sbt scalafmtAll`.

tasks.title: Simplify FlowAuthoring.extractApiMaterial to a plain write into the fresh sandbox
tasks.description: Issue #196 item 6, fourth bullet. `extractApiMaterial` is only ever called with the cache of a sandbox `AuthoringSandbox.create` just created, so the completeness check and the per-file temp-and-move can never trigger. Reduce it to `os.makeDir.all(dir)` plus one `os.write(dir / name, PromptResource.load(...))` per bundled name; delete `isComplete` and `writeAtomically`; rewrite the scaladoc to the present contract (fresh directory, three static files) without history. Delete the `FlowAuthoringTest` cases "is idempotent" and "self-heals a half-populated leftover dir"; keep "writes the three bundled files, matching resources". Run `sbt "shell/test"` and `sbt scalafmtAll`.

resultJson.brief:
## Modules and dependency order
`tools` (standalone: LLM SPI, events, `OrcaDir`, `AttemptId`, `ConfigHome`, MCP hosts) ← `flow` (stages, progress log, sessions, `FeatureBranch`, `AgentSpec`) ← `runner` (`flow()` entry in `runner/src/main/scala/orca/flowEntry.scala`, `FlowLifecycle`, `OrcaLog`, attempt manifest) ← `shell` (CLI, session picker, built-in flows, authoring). Backends `claude/ codex/ gemini/ opencode/ pi/` depend only on `tools`. Anything both `flow` and `runner` need (e.g. a `BackendTag` JSON codec) must live in `tools`.

Read `AGENTS.md` first: "What a run writes to disk" (lines ~262-310) is the authoritative table of every file orca creates; update its rows whenever a path or its remover changes. `.orca/reviewers/orca.md` lists the review rules applied to every Scala change here. Invoke the `direct-style-scala` skill before writing Scala.

## Build / test / style
- `sbt test`, `sbt "<module>/test"`, `sbt "<module>/testOnly <fqcn>"`; `sbt scalafmtAll` before finishing; never `sbt clean`; zero warnings (`-Wunused:all`, `-Wvalue-discard`, `-Wnonunit-statement` — use `val _ =` for discarded values). Never commit.
- Braceless syntax, explicit return types on public members, intentional visibility (`private[orca]` etc.), no class-level `var`, no default values on persisted/domain fields, no back-compat machinery, no history in comments ("no longer", "renamed from"), no plan/epic labels in comments, scaladoc = contract, `//` = non-obvious why. Tests: one scenario each; fixtures `orca.testkit.TempDirs.dir()`, `GitRepo.seeded()`, `StubGitHubTool`, `PushlessGit`.
- Every write under `.orca/` goes through an `OrcaDir.ensure*` accessor; prefer `os.write` (CREATE_NEW) over `os.write.over`. `.orca/cache/` self-ignores (`.gitignore` = `*`).
- Dated docs (`adr/*` amendments, `docs/research/*`, `docs/superpowers/plans/*`) are left alone; only undated prose (AGENTS.md, README, scaladoc) follows a rename.

## BackendTag today (item 1)
- `tools/src/main/scala/orca/agents/BackendTag.scala`: `enum BackendTag(val wireName: String)` with cases `ClaudeCode, Codex, Opencode, Pi, Gemini` whose wireName equals the case name; `object BackendTag { def fromWireName(name: String): Option[BackendTag] }`. Same file holds `SessionId`/`WireSessionId` (keep).
- Emission: `tools/src/main/scala/orca/agents/TurnAccounting.scala:65` `sessionCommitted()` builds `OrcaEvent.SessionCommitted(harness = backend.tag.wireName, clientId, wireId: Option[String], sessionKey: Option[SessionKey], agent, role)` — event defined at `tools/src/main/scala/orca/events/OrcaEvent.scala:148`.
- Manifest: `runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/manifest/AttemptManifest.scala` — `ManifestSession(harness: String, wireId, agent, role, stage, minted: Option[SessionKey], lastActiveAt)`; `AttemptManifest.codec` derived with `JsonData.strictCodecConfig`. The proven pattern for a nested enum codec is `AttemptStatus`: `given codec: ConfiguredJsonValueCodec[AttemptStatus] = ConfiguredJsonValueCodec.derived(using CodecMakerConfig.withDiscriminatorFieldName(None))` in the companion — cases serialise as plain strings, which for `BackendTag` keeps today's on-disk spelling. `AttemptManifestWriter.scala` (`ManifestState.withSession`) dedups on `(harness, conversationKey)`.
- Session records: `SessionRecord(name, stage, id, seed, resumeWireId: Option[String], backend: Option[String])` at `flow/src/main/scala/orca/sessions/SessionStore.scala:35`, codec `OsSessionStore.codec` derived with `withTransientNone(false)`. Built in `flow/src/main/scala/orca/Session.scala`: `reuseOrMint` (:212, compares `agent.backendTag.map(_.wireName)` to `recorded.backend`, `warnBackendSwap(fc, key, recordedTag: String, currentTag: Option[String])`), `mintSession` (:279), `persistResumeWireId` (:382, "heals" the tag). `Agent.backendTag: Option[BackendTag]`.
- Readers with an "unknown harness" branch: `runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/FlowLifecycle.scala:137-168` (`rehydrateSessions` + `targetAgent`; `AgentSet.agentFor(tag: BackendTag): Agent[?]` at `flow/src/main/scala/orca/AgentSet.scala:34` is total), `shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/sessions/ResumeCommand.scala:23-37` (`wireIdAndTag`, `staticGate`, `build` uses `AgentSpec.harnessNameFor.getOrElse(tag, s.harness)`), `shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/sessions/SessionPicker.scala:244` (`harnessSettingsName(wireName: String)`, callers `ContinueCli.scala:70`, `cli/Tables.scala:81`, `Main.scala:738`; `SessionRow.harness` stays a settings-name `String` for the JSON listing).
- `flow/src/main/scala/orca/settings/AgentSpec.scala`: `harnessNames: Map[String, BackendTag]` (settings spellings `claude`, `codex`, …) and `harnessNameFor: Map[BackendTag, String] = harnessNames.map(_.swap)` — a Map apply is not compile-checked; an exhaustive `match` from tag to name, with `harnessNames` derived from it, makes the reverse total.
- Other `.wireName` users: `tools/src/main/scala/orca/agents/EnforcementNotice.scala:80`, `runner/src/test/scala/orca/runner/EnforcementTableTest.scala:218,237` (renders the AGENTS.md enforcement table header; `.toString` gives the same spelling, so the table in AGENTS.md is unchanged), `runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/LoggingListener.scala:56` (just logs it).
- Tests/fixtures pinned to strings: `tools/src/test/scala/orca/agents/BackendTagCodecTest.scala` (delete), `BaseAgentTest.scala:438`, `AgentCallSessionCommittedTest.scala:72`, `runner/src/test/scala/orca/runner/FlowLifecycleTest.scala:1649-1718` (`backend = Some("Codex")`, and the "unknown backend tag … warns loudly (6B.1)" test to delete), `flow/src/test/scala/orca/{SessionTest,FlowSessionTest,CommitMessageTest,review/ReviewAndFixTest,sessions/SessionStoreTest}.scala` `SessionRecord(...)` literals, `shell/src/test/scala/orca/shell/sessions/ManifestFixtures.scala` (`harness: String = "ClaudeCode"`), `ManifestRoundTripTest.scala` (harness `"claude"`), `cli/CliTest.scala:1249`, `MainTest.scala:401` ("falls back to the raw harness string" — delete), `ResumeCommandTest.scala:92` ("unrecognised harness string is not resumable" — delete). GOTCHA: `runner/src/test/scala/orca/runner/manifest/AttemptManifestWriterTest.scala:65-69` seeds pruning tests with raw JSON containing `"harness":"claude"`; under a strict enum codec that manifest fails to decode and counts as NOT continuable (`AttemptPruning.continuableManifest`), silently changing what the pruning tests assert — respell it `ClaudeCode`. `ManifestReaderTest.scala:181` ("list skips a manifest with an unrecognised outcome, warning by filename") is the precedent for decode-time rejection; `ManifestReader.readManifest` turns a `JsonFile.Read` failure into a warning naming the file.
- Prose naming wireName: `BackendTag` scaladoc, `SessionStore.scala:25-33` scaladoc, `AgentSpec.scala:13-15`, `SessionPicker.scala:239-243`, `ResumeCommand.scala:48-50`, AGENTS.md ~lines 204-208 ("a tag matching none of the context's accessors is skipped, not guessed").

## Attempt files, manifest writer, pruning (items 2, 4)
- `tools/src/main/scala/orca/AttemptId.scala`: `private[orca] opaque type AttemptId = String` spelled `<startedAt epoch ms>-<pid>`; `AttemptId(startedAt: Instant, pid: Long)`, `parse`, `.value`.
- `tools/src/main/scala/orca/OrcaDir.scala`: `ManifestSuffix = ".manifest.json"`, `CostLogSuffix = ".cost.jsonl"`, `attemptsPath`/`ensureAttempts`, `manifestPath(workDir, id)`, `costLogPath`, `attemptIdOf(file): Option[AttemptId]` — strips a known suffix from the file name then `AttemptId.parse`; unknown names (in-flight dot-temp files) map to `None`. `OrcaDirTest.scala` exists in tools.
- `runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/manifest/AttemptManifestWriter.scala`: `AttemptManifestWriter.start(workDir, orcaVersion, flowName, pid, clock)(using Ox, BufferCapacity)`; `AttemptManifestWriterState` computes `startedAt = clock()` and `attemptId = AttemptId(startedAt, pid)` at construction, calls `OrcaDir.ensureAttempts`, writes the first manifest, then `AttemptPruning.prune(attemptsDir)`; `finish(outcome: AttemptOutcome)`; `statusOf(AttemptOutcome): AttemptStatus` widens. `AttemptOutcome { Succeeded, Failed }` is declared in this file; `AttemptStatus { Running, Succeeded, Failed }` in `AttemptManifest.scala`. Tests construct `AttemptManifestWriterState` directly via `newWriter(workDir, clock, flowName)` with `fixedClock(instants*)` whose FIRST instant becomes `startedAt` (`AttemptManifestWriterTest.scala:30-45`); `shell/.../ManifestRoundTripTest.scala` and `CostLogTest.scala` use `start(...)`.

## Gemini settings (item 6c)
`GeminiSettings.register(workDir, mcpUrl): AutoCloseable` writes `<workDir>/.gemini/settings.json` with `os.write.over(..., createFolders = true)` and on close restores the original bytes or removes the file; it never records whether `.gemini/` existed. Orca's own stage commits (`Flow.recordAndCommit`, `git.commit`'s `add -A`) run after a turn's conversation has finalised (one gemini process per turn; `Chat` handles are `InStage`-only), so only a commit the agent itself makes mid-turn can sweep the modified file — a residual to state in the scaladoc, not fix. Tests in `gemini/src/test/scala/orca/tools/gemini/GeminiSettingsTest.scala` (`settingsFile(workDir)` helper, "close removes the file again when it did not exist before").
